title: Atmospheric Temp & Monsoon Extremes (1980–2025)
source: NASA POWER (MERRA-2) & GPM IMERG Satellite Archive
coords: LAT: 12.97° N | LON: 77.59° E (SOUTH ASIA MONSOON CORE)

records.explanation: 1980 Pre-GPM Baseline: Calm 26.8°C regional average with steady 38mm monsoon precipitation.
1985 Baseline: Stable 27.1°C temperature with moderate 42mm monsoon rain.
1988 La Niña Surge: Heavy monsoon trough brings 58.4mm intense regional downpours.
1990: Slight warming (+0.3°C). Pitch rises gently with light rain harmonics.
1994 Positive Indian Ocean Dipole: Moisture convergence boosts cloudburst intensity.
1995: Noticeable thermal shift to 27.9°C; heavier 68mm cloudbursts trigger brighter chime.
1998 Super El Niño Anomaly: Sharp +0.6°C thermal spike triggers mid-high harmonic alert.
2000: Millennial baseline reaches 28.2°C; mid-frequency synth tone stabilizes.
2005 Extreme Cloudburst: Sharp jump to 94.5mm extreme rain! High-pitch raindrop arpeggio activates.
2010 El Niño Effect: 29.3°C heat pushes pitch higher with louder storm resonance.
2015 Record Heat: Near 30°C threshold. High-frequency alert harmonics engage.
2018 Severe Flooding Epoch: GPM IMERG records 139.2mm convective burst.
2020 Extreme Event: 145mm flash rain burst creates rapid high-pitch acoustic shimmer.
2023 Thermal Record: 30.6°C land-atmosphere coupling drives extreme monsoon volatility.
2025 Peak Anomaly: +4.1°C above 1980 baseline. Maximum pitch & full harmonic intensity.
